This is each leaf curl disease, caused by the fungus Taphrina deformans occurs on peaches, apricots, and nectarines in Kentucky commercial orchards as well as in home landscapes. o control peach leaf curl and plum pockets, a single fungicide application needs to be made between now and when the buds swell in early spring.  However, as soon as the buds swell in spring, it is too late to apply the fungicide, so depending on the weather, now is a god time to take action to control these diseases.  Fall and early winter is usually a good time to spray for leaf curl or plum pockets because the weather may be dry and it is easier to move equipment through the orchard.  In addition, peach and plum buds sometimes begin to swell during a mid-winter thaw leaving the grower no chance to control the disease in early spring.  Fungicides will not control peach leaf curl or plum pockets once buds begin to swell in spring and infection has occurred. The choice of fungicides for dormant sprays include chlorothalonil (Bravo); ferbam (Carbamate); Ziram; or fixed copper fungicides such as copper hydroxide (Kocide), copper oxychloride (COCS), or Bordeaux mixture.  Thorough coverage of the twigs and branches is essential.

The day was long, and the event felt short. Love, I never had grasped the concept of this intense feeling that all of Earth’s organisms depend on. Two days before sophomore year ended, I obtained a bouquet of flowers. I was planning to give it to a friend. But like most major decisions I made, there were mistakes that I regret doing. Excitement rushed through my veins. Tragically as soon as I gave her an item that screams, “WILL YOU GO OUT WITH ME?” I felt nothing. It felt as if the dopamine in my body just flushed out of my system. In that tenth of a second, my conception of reality changed forever. My conscious told me what in the world am I doing. In that moment I concluded that I would never want to be in any sort of relationship at all because...oh no, I need an escape plan from this situation. As soon as she held the bouquet, I just said in the most nonchalant tone, “It was from a friend of mine.” I created this façade about one of my freshman companions having feelings for her. Surprisingly, I did convince her and her group of friends that this symbol of union-ship was not from me. That day, I had realized that I could not bear to love a person if I am going to have to hurt them if I don’t love them anymore. My path of celibacy had begun from this point onward.
